title: Lightweaver — Mirror Lab Puzzle

checks.name: geometry and puzzle test suite
checks.details: 121 assertions, 0 failures. Covers ray/segment intersection (distance, parameter, behind-ray, out-of-span, parallel rejection, endpoint inclusivity), ray/circle, reflection (normal incidence, 45 degree case, angle-in equals angle-out, length preservation, involution), refraction (Snell verified numerically, unit output, TIR either side of the critical angle, blue deviating more than red), the epsilon self-collision rule in both its parametric and geometric halves, attenuation monotonicity, and prism vertex geometry.

checks.name: engine termination and determinism
checks.details: A ray trapped between two parallel mirrors terminates on the 22-bounce cap in under 2 seconds with no degenerate zero-length segments. Repeated traces of the same level produce byte-identical beam arrays. Walls block, splitters emit two children, filters mask to a single channel, and a prism yields exactly three wavelengths.

checks.name: all five levels solvable and non-trivial
checks.details: For each of the 5 levels: the start state is not already solved, the published solution does solve it, no watcher is tripped by the solution, the segment budget is not exhausted, every plate clears its intensity threshold, and the solve survives plus/minus 1 unit and plus/minus 1 degree jitter on every solution piece. Coverage assertions confirm sources, mirrors, walls, filters, splitters, prisms, targets and sensors are all used, that a level needs splitting or dispersion, that a level needs sensor avoidance, and that a level needs two colours mixed into one plate.

checks.name: rotation lattice reachability
checks.command: node -e '<levels.js check: every solution angle minus start angle is a multiple of 15>'
checks.details: Every solution angle differs from its start angle by a multiple of 15 degrees, so the Q/E rotation increment alone can reach every solution without needing fine Shift rotation.

checks.name: level definitions immutable under tracing
checks.command: node -e '<repeated trace + JSON compare of levels.js definitions>'
checks.details: Tracing a level does not mutate the shared level definition, and repeated traces of freshly cloned levels stay byte-identical.

checks.name: syntax check of all scripts
checks.command: node --check app.js && node --check engine.js && node --check levels.js && node --check test-geometry.js

checks.name: renders from file:// with active beams
checks.details: Opened directly from disk at 1600x900 and screenshotted. Level 1 shows three live reflected segments, the source, both mirrors, walls, the red plate and the full panel chrome. Levels 2 through 5 were screenshotted the same way: level 2 shows the beam splitting and both filtered branches (13 segments), level 3 shows the prism fanning white into separated red, green and blue rays onto three plates, level 4 shows both watchers and the green beam, level 5 shows all three sources with the watcher tripped and the alarm card visible.

checks.name: end-to-end interaction under synthetic input
checks.command: '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome' --headless=new --window-size=1600,900 --virtual-time-budget=4000 --screenshot=qa.png 'file://$PWD/qa.html'  (temporary harness dispatching real KeyboardEvent/PointerEvent at the live app; harness removed afterwards)
checks.details: Verified against the running app: Tab cycles selection; E rotates in 15 degree steps and reaching 135 degrees triggers victory with the move count and best score shown; Z undoes back to 105 degrees and clears victory; Y redoes and restores it; R resets to the start pose with moves back to 0; a synthetic pointerdown/move/up drag moved a mirror from (900,150) to (830,210) with 5-unit snapping; arrow keys nudged (830,210) to (820,205) and coalesced into a single move; H advanced the hint text through stage 1 to stage 3 and capped there; number keys switched levels; and localStorage persisted {"1":{"solved":true,"best":1}} from file://, with the solved chip and the 1/5 counter updating.

checks.name: victory presentation
checks.details: The completion card reports move count and best, the solved beam path stays visible through the deliberately sheer overlay, and the lit plate renders its expanding shockwave rings. A window error listener recorded no runtime errors during the solve.

checks.name: no remote runtime references
checks.command: grep -nEi "https?://|//cdn|fonts\.google|integrity=|\.woff|import[ (]" index.html styles.css app.js engine.js levels.js
checks.details: No matches. The only external references in index.html are the three relative classic script tags and one relative stylesheet link. Fonts are system stacks only; there are no remote assets, no ES module imports (which would break file://), and no network calls.

summary: A direct-open Canvas 2D optical puzzle. engine.js is a pure, deterministic ray engine — Cramer's-rule segment intersection, normal-based reflection, vector Snell refraction with per-channel indices for real prism dispersion, half-silvered splitters, single-channel filters, absorbing walls, exponential distance attenuation, and a two-part epsilon strategy backed by bounce, segment and intensity caps so no path can loop. levels.js holds five handcrafted puzzles as pure data, including one built around splitting, one around prism dispersion, one around avoiding forbidden watcher sensors, and one that needs red and green mixed into a single amber plate. app.js renders a dark instrument board with additive three-pass beam bloom, geometric target apertures and glass-and-metal pieces, and supplies drag, knob and wheel rotation, Q/E and arrow precision controls, undo/redo, reset, three-stage hints that stop short of solving, level switching, colour-and-intensity victory detection with a completion animation and move count, localStorage progress, resize that never touches puzzle geometry, reduced-motion support, and visible focus with textual control labels. test-geometry.js runs 121 dependency-free assertions over the geometry primitives, engine invariants, colour scoring and all five levels.
known_issues: A burst of Q/E or arrow presses on one piece within 700 ms is intentionally counted as a single move, so best-move scores are more forgiving of fine keyboard adjustment than of equivalent discrete drags.

Level 1 performs one automatic legal rotation about a second after load to demonstrate that pieces turn. It counts as a move and is undoable, so a run left untouched for a few seconds starts from a move count of 1.
Interaction was verified with synthetic PointerEvents in headless Chrome rather than by hand on a touchscreen; multi-touch gestures are untested.
